evidence_policy.observation: Directly visible in a pinned repository source or commit.
evidence_policy.reproduction: A behavior reproduced with a bounded executable fixture.
evidence_policy.inference: A conclusion derived from one or more observations; supporting premises are named.
evidence_policy.proposal: A recommended future design or action; not represented as current truth.
evidence_policy.unknown: Not established by the accessible evidence and intentionally left unresolved.

limitations: The GitHub connector exposed source and commit history but not arbitrary SQL execution against the published SQLite release assets.
Published row counts are repository claims and were not independently re-counted in this audit.
Small SQLite behavior checks were reproduced with synthetic databases by the accompanying verifier.

sources.scope: Initial public schema, loaders, query surface, README, and graph design claims.
Initial public Book Library builders, README, locator, and graph integration.
Extraction queue views and measured queue counts.
Measured finding that question exports lacked dereferenceable evidence.
Durable identity, Release, Snapshot, Event, and Source Inventory boundaries.
Question-first research loop, evidence objects, assumptions, and stopping rules.
Immutable release, integrity, artifact, and distribution contract.

findings.title: V2 builder resolves the schema from the wrong directory

evidence.observation: The path is constructed from the loaders directory and the filename people_schema_v2.sql.
The actual schema file is stored under schema/, not loaders/.

findings.implication: A clean checkout cannot execute the documented V2 build path without an unrecorded local modification.
findings.recommended_action: Resolve from repository root and add a clean-checkout smoke test.

findings.title: Descriptive attributes can become near-certain identity evidence

evidence.observation: real_name, website, company, and location are written to external_ids alongside issuer identifiers.
Every repeated (platform, value) group is processed by the shared_external_id method at confidence 0.98, with no allowlist.

reproduction.expected_current_result: no issuer-unique allowlist detected; 100 repeated attributes imply 4950 candidate pairs

findings.implication: People sharing a common employer, city, name, or organization website can be proposed as the same actor with near-certain confidence.
findings.recommended_action: Separate identifiers from attributes and allow automatic identity evidence only for documented issuer-unique identifiers.

findings.title: Accepted identity claims are not applied by the query surface

evidence.observation: identity_claim supports proposed, accepted, and rejected states.
No query reads identity_claim; works chooses the raw name match with the greatest content count.

findings.implication: Review decisions do not create a query-visible canonical actor or aggregate accepted source records.
findings.recommended_action: Introduce accepted source-actor assignments and make all actor queries consume a canonical projection.

findings.title: The V2 build silently merges book people by normalized name

evidence.observation: Book people are assigned to an existing person ID when the lowercased whitespace-normalized name already exists.
A second direct-write integration also matches existing graph people by normalized name.

findings.implication: Name-only merging bypasses the explicit claim and reversal model and leaves two integration paths with different schema assumptions.
findings.recommended_action: Ingest source actors independently, resolve through one policy, and retire direct source-library writes into graph internals.

findings.title: rank_score stores incompatible and non-idempotent values

evidence.observation: Book work count and inherited V1 score are loaded into rank_score.
Summed repository stars are loaded into rank_score.
Average model-rated repository value is added to the existing rank_score, so repeat runs can add it again.
GitHub follower count later replaces rank_score.

findings.implication: The field has no stable unit or interpretation and cannot support reproducible cross-domain ranking.
findings.recommended_action: Store typed metric observations with source, time, unit, and method version; derive named rankings.

findings.title: The qualified FTS MATCH expression fails and is silently bypassed

evidence.observation: who() uses WHERE people.person_search MATCH ? and catches all sqlite3.Error exceptions.

reproduction.expected_current_result: qualified_query_error=no such column: people.person_search; corrected query returns the fixture row

findings.implication: Name queries fall back to a linear LIKE scan while appearing to support FTS.
findings.recommended_action: Use the valid FTS table expression and add a test that proves the FTS branch executed.

findings.title: The works query overstates completeness and hides truncation

evidence.observation: works() selects one heuristic match, limits to 200 rows, and reports count=len(returned rows) without total or truncation.

findings.implication: An agent can interpret a partial, unresolved source view as everything the human produced.
findings.recommended_action: Declare source coverage, identity status, total matches, returned rows, truncation, and known gaps.

findings.title: Person topics are stronger than the underlying source assertion

evidence.observation: LCSH work subjects are rolled directly into person_topic.
Repository topics and programming languages are rolled directly into person_topic.

findings.implication: Work classification can be misread as actor expertise, endorsement, or belief, especially across non-author roles.
findings.recommended_action: Preserve work-level classification and expose actor output profiles as named derivations with role and scheme visible.

findings.title: Lifetime overlap is presented as stronger intellectual adjacency

evidence.observation: v_contemporaries computes overlapping lifespan intervals and substitutes birth_year + 80 when death year is absent.
The example describes results as the actual historical conversation.

findings.implication: Possible temporal coexistence can be mistaken for contact, influence, or shared discourse.
findings.recommended_action: Rename as possible lifetime overlap and expose source, precision, and estimation flags.

findings.title: The canonical entity is broader than a person

evidence.observation: The person.kind enum contains human, organisation, pseudonym, and unknown.
GitHub owners can be organizations or unknown.
Inherited V1 rows are hardcoded to kind=human.

findings.implication: Projects, collectives, organizations, bots, personas, and shared accounts are forced into an inconsistent person abstraction.
findings.recommended_action: Use an internal actor abstraction and model accounts separately from the actor controlling them.

findings.title: The data-release reproducibility contract is incomplete

evidence.observation: The comment states that release assets can be replaced.
The current wall clock is stored in fetched_at for every build.
The README says locator.sqlite records SHA-256 per book.
The checked-in location schema has no digest column and the builder records offsets and lengths only.
The Great Library requires immutable releases, artifact revisions, and integrity state.

findings.implication: The documented ability to rebuild or verify an exact data release is not yet fully represented by the checked-in builders and manifests.
findings.recommended_action: Pin source snapshots and clocks, publish builder receipts and checksums, and create successor releases rather than replacing bytes.

findings.title: Book extraction profile SQL does not match its stated deduplication and section policy

evidence.observation: Core and tier-two policies compare one-letter values to bookcase, while the builder creates two-letter bookcases for classes such as QA.
v_extraction_queue uses UNION on rows containing different reason values, allowing one GID to remain multiple times.

findings.implication: Books can be omitted from intended section-level profiles and can appear more than once in a queue described as deduplicated.
findings.recommended_action: Filter by section for section-level policy and aggregate membership reasons under one profile row per GID.

findings.title: Question-addressable summaries are not yet dereferenceable evidence

evidence.observation: The evaluated export contained model summaries but no URL, quotation, or citation and therefore did not replace a manual evidence link.

findings.implication: A large indexed corpus and generated summaries do not yet form a source-grounded research answer system.
findings.recommended_action: Require exact artifact and source-span receipts for accepted claims.

findings.title: Automated repository contracts are absent from the initial public implementation

evidence.observation: The commit file list contains schema, loaders, README, and .gitignore but no tests or workflow files.

findings.implication: Parallel loader work can silently change build, identity, idempotence, and query semantics.
findings.recommended_action: Add clean-build, identity, idempotence, query, release, and privacy fixtures before broad ingestion.

architectural_decisions_proposed.decision: Separate immutable source actors from opaque canonical actors.
Represent canonicalization as evidenced source-actor assignments rather than destructive or silent merges.
Replace rank_score with typed, time-bound metric observations and derive named projections.
Separate Work, expression/version, artifact, locator, and contribution semantics.
Model public statements with exact source spans; treat beliefs as uncertain derived projections only.

unknowns.question: What is the measured false-positive and false-negative rate of each identity method on representative full-scale data?
What exact bytes and checksums are currently served by each published release asset, and have any assets been replaced?
What are the current full-dataset row counts after rebuilding from pinned source snapshots?
Which source family yields the greatest answer-value increase after identity, rights, and maintenance cost?
Which query patterns justify a graph traversal service beyond the portable SQLite snapshot?
